title: Hosted API autoscaler thrash -> streaming fallthrough incident digest
content:
Summary:

On 2026-08-11 at ~14:12 UTC a production traffic pattern change (customer-driven burst + regional failover) triggered an autoscaler thrash in the eu-central GPU pool. The autoscaler oscillation caused rapid model instance churn and repeated model swaps on the serving tier; as a result, a subset of streaming requests entered a fallthrough path which led to session truncation and a ~6 minute window of elevated client 5xxs (stream disconnects) and token-level latency spikes.

Impact:
- Duration: ~14:12 UTC -> ~14:28 UTC (~16 minutes).
- User-visible: ~1.8% of total hosted-api streaming sessions during window experienced abrupt disconnects or incomplete streams; non-streaming generation endpoints experienced increased tail latency but few direct 5xxs.
- SLOs impacted: streaming success rate target missed for a 15-minute window in eu-central; overall hosted-api error budget not exhausted.
- Systems: serving runtime (model-swapping orchestration), autoscaler controller for Dedicated GPU pool (eu-central-1), streaming session manager.

How we detected it:
- Grafana alert: streaming-session-error-rate-eu spiked at 14:15 UTC (alert fired).
- On-call page: pager triggered for SRE on-call (alert SRE-Streaming-ErrRate).
- Slack from customer success reporting several customers with aborted streams.

What happened (chronology / timeline):
- 14:11:55 UTC: sudden traffic surge in eu-central region due to batch of customer retries after upstream client backoff misconfiguration (customer-side).
- 14:12:10 UTC: autoscaler observed sustained high GPU utilization and started scale-up, following configured aggressive policy for peak bursts.
- 14:13:05 UTC: scale actions began returning new nodes, but a concurrent capacity reclaim (cloud provider preemption signal in one AZ) returned mixed signals; autoscaler controller retried and subsequently issued a scale-down request to rebalance across AZs.
- 14:13:40 UTC: scale-down requests hit the same node group that still had in-flight streaming sessions; orchestration triggered model swap operations to drain and reassign sessions.
- 14:14:05 -> 14:18:00 UTC: repeated node add/remove cycles (thrash) caused the serving runtime to attempt model swaps multiple times for the same session. The streaming session manager did not have an idempotent, resumable handover path for sessions while model weights were being reloaded, causing some clients to see aborts.
- 14:15:00 UTC: Grafana alert fired for streaming-session-error-rate-eu. On-call paged.
- 14:17:30 UTC: SRE team applied two mitigations (1) temporarily set autoscaler cooldown window to 6 minutes (mitigated thrash), (2) rolled safe-mode flag on model-orchestration to prefer draining nodes rather than immediate swaps.
- 14:20:00 UTC: error rate trending down, by 14:28 UTC system returned to normal.

Root cause analysis (summary):
- Primary root cause: Autoscaler configuration allowed rapid scale-up/scale-down cycles when the provider signalled mixed capacity events; this interacted poorly with our serving runtime’s model swap protocol leading to session aborts.
- Contributing factors:
  - Serving runtime does not fully support resumable streaming handoffs across in-flight model swaps. There is a race between drain/evict and the session manager that leads to client disconnects when a model process is restarted mid-session.
  - Autoscaler cooldown and stabilization settings were tuned for aggressive responsiveness in prod to handle flash bursts; those settings are too permissive for workloads with long-lived streaming connections.
  - Lack of a safety gate in orchestration that detects repeated swaps for the same session (no swap-threshold to block flip-flopping).
  - Observability gap: we did not have a metric that correlates model-swap frequency per-session; existing alerts were based on session error rate rather than swap activity.

Immediate mitigations applied (timeline and commands):
- Increase autoscaler cooldown: set AUTOSCALER_COOLDOWN to 360s for eu-central nodepool. (Applied 14:17 UTC): kubectl patch configmap autoscaler -n infra --patch '{"data":{"cooldown_s":"360"}}'
- Enable orchestration safe-mode flag (prefer drain): POST /admin/flags model_orch_safe_mode=true (internal admin UI)
- Temporarily added rule in edge/router to prefer returning cached responses for known long-lived sessions while backend stabilizes (edge fallback).
- Opened emergency MR to add swap-threshold guard in serving runtime: GH#9821 (merged 14:46 UTC into canary) — this was a short-term code guard but the heavyweight fix requires additional testing.

Why this was not prevented by existing runbooks/automation:
- Runbook for autop-scaling incidents assumed stateless inference endpoints; streaming sessions were considered a normal traffic shape but not explicitly covered.
- No playbook step existed to correlate frequent model swaps to streaming error spikes; operators followed error-rate playbook which drove scaling changes rather than throttling.
- No automated circuit breaker between autoscaler and model-orchestration to prevent flip-flop during cloud provider capacity events.

Action items / follow-ups (owners + SLA):
- Short-term (P0->P1):
  1) Adjust autoscaler config for all streaming-capable nodepools to cooldown >= 300s by 2026-08-14. Owner: Marcus Rivera.
  2) Add metric and dashboard: model_swap_rate_per_session, and an alert when swap-rate > 1 in 5m. Owner: Lina Chen. ETA 2026-08-16.
  3) Implement swap-threshold guard in serving runtime to block repeated swaps for the same session (backport guard to stable release). Owner: Priya Nair. ETA 2026-08-18.

- Medium-term (P1):
  4) Implement resumable streaming handoff protocol so sessions can continue on new model workers after swap (design doc). Owner: Eng-Serving-Runtime (TBD). ETA 2026-10-01.
  5) Autoscaler / orchestration contract: introduce hysteresis and preemption-awareness to prefer draining existing nodes over immediate removal. Owner: Platform-Engineering. ETA 2026-09-01.
  6) Update incident runbooks to include streaming-specific steps (playbook branch: streaming-thrash). Owner: eng-sre. ETA 2026-08-20.

- Long-term (P2):
  7) Rework multi-AZ scaling policy to avoid oscillation when the provider signals partial AZ pressure. Owner: infra-cloud-team. ETA 2026-11-01.

Runbook gaps identified (to be patched):
- No documented safe autoscale thresholds for streaming; update runbook with example knobs per SKU.
- No established test harness for repeated model swap churn against streaming sessions. Need load test and simulation harness.
- Alerting only on error rate; absent an early-warning alert for model-swap frequency.

Customer comms notes:
- CS drafted a short note to customers in eu-central who saw retries: apologize + explain transient scaling event; indicate mitigation steps and ETA for durable fixes. Ticket ref: CS-INC-718.

Open tickets / next steps (quick links):
- JIRA SRE-1837: Investigate autoscaler policy and add cooldown default for streaming nodepools.
- JIRA INFR-2098: Add swap-rate metric and dashboard.
- GH PR repo/redwood-inference#9821: swap-threshold guard (short-term patch).
- Confluence: "Hosted API: Streaming incident playbook" — draft to be created and linked.

Notes to self / raw observations (informal):
- Observed repeated logs: "model_swap: session=abc123 worker=X -> worker=Y reason=scale_down" repeated 5x over 90s for same session token. That's the smoking gun.
- Edge fallback was useful but brittle; evaluate whether we should more aggressively serve cached partial responses rather than abort when we detect backend swap.
- Customer retries were unnecessary; maybe add guidance to customers to exponential backoff more aggressively or implement server-side retry smoothing.

Suggested immediate runbook patch (text for doc):
- When streaming error-rate alert fires in a region:
  1) Query model_swap_rate_per_session (if metric missing, run quick log query: "model_swap.*session=.*count > 1 in 5m")
  2) If swap_rate > threshold: set autoscaler cooldown to 300s and enable model_orch_safe_mode true.
  3) If provider preemption events present, disable immediate scale-down across affected nodepool until ops confirms capacity.
  4) Notify CS to throttle customer retries for top-5 active clients.

Appendix (diagnostic snippets):
- Example log query (prod-logs):
  resource.type=container AND jsonPayload.msg: "model_swap" AND jsonPayload.session_id:*
- Quick kubectl command used to patch cooldown:
  kubectl patch configmap autoscaler -n infra --patch '{"data":{"cooldown_s":"360"}}'

Conclusion:
This was a classic interaction bug: two well-intentioned systems (responsive autoscaling + aggressive model orchestration for low-latency) combined to create instability for a workload pattern we had not guarded against. Fixing requires both policy changes (hysteresis for streaming workloads) and engineering work to make streaming sessions resilient to model worker churn.

-- Ethan
